title: Fetch-decode-execute card sort
subject: Computing
source: Seeded from computing/y9 lesson 6 (Fetch-decode-execute card sort (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 6: The CPU and the fetch-decode-execute cycle. To understand how the CPU carries out instructions using the fetch-decode-execute cycle

questions.q: Describe the fetch stage in two sentences.
questions.a: The address in the PC is copied to the MAR and the instruction at that address is fetched from RAM into the MDR. The PC is increased by 1.
questions.model: Teacher writes it in two sentences, naming each register as it is used.

questions.q: Which part of the CPU adds two numbers?
Core: Put the 6 cards of the cycle in order and write one sentence for each stage (worksheet).
questions.a: PC to MAR; fetch to MDR; PC + 1; decode in CU; execute; repeat.
questions.model: Teacher places card 1 (PC address copied to MAR) and explains it.

questions.q: Extend: Explain why doubling the cores does not always double the speed.
questions.a: Some tasks cannot be split into parts that run at the same time, and cores share memory.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why cache makes a CPU faster.
questions.a: Cache stores frequently used data close to the CPU, so it waits less for slower RAM.

questions.q: The stages in order are... A) decode, fetch, execute B) fetch, decode, execute C) execute, fetch, decode
Big question: what is the CPU doing in each cycle?
questions.a: Fetching an instruction from memory, decoding it and executing it.
